facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Arcosa's net leverage was 1.91x at 30 June 2026 on a continuing-operations basis, but that figure reflects barge sale cash held on the balance sheet, not earnings growth, so the creditor cushion is only as durable as that cash. Only USD 83.0 million of the USD 429.9 million net sale proceeds repaid debt, leaving USD 432.1 million of cash against USD 1,436.7 million of carrying debt, with a pro forma net leverage of 1.92x after the dividend paid on 31 July 2026. Continuing operations used USD 68.9 million of cash in the first half after capital expenditures, and cash interest cover for 2026 cannot be stated because the quarterly reports give no interest paid. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against the cautious reading is the size of the cash buffer: USD 432.1 million of cash and a USD 700.0 million revolver with no loans outstanding cover the 2029 notes of USD 400.0 million, and net debt fell by USD 303.6 million in six months. rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: no source is dated after 2026-08-05, so every ratio, balance and the merger outcome stop at 2026-06-30; the third-quarter report and the merger documents would close it. - High: the 2025 annual report includes the barge business (revenue of 383.3, EBITDA of 53.6) while the 2026 quarterly reports and their 2025 comparatives exclude it; the last-twelve-months figures therefore use a 2025 year rebuilt from the segment note, which is a calculation, not a company figure; a recast annual statement would close it. - High: the covenant leverage ratio, its EBITDA definition and the interest cover test level are not printed, so covenant headroom is not calculable; the credit agreement and Amendment No. 3 dated 2026-07-29 would close it. - Medium: no cash interest paid is stated for the interim periods, so EBITDA over cash interest is not calculable for 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 and the proxy on interest expense is shown instead; the third-quarter cash flow statement or a supplemental disclosure would close it. - Medium: the undrawn revolver amount and letters of credit are not stated at 2026-06-30, and the undrawn amount at 2023-12-31 is not stated, so those two liquidity cells are not supplied; the March 2026 statement of 700.0 is the latest. - Medium: the issuer states no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or add-backs, so the EBITDA bridge is not stated and EBITDA is derived from operating profit and depreciation, depletion, and amortization; no source states a covenant EBITDA. - Medium: the effect on net debt of the merger agreement, Amendment No. 3 and the proxy statement is not stated, so the post-balance-sheet table carries only the dividend of 2.5 paid on 2026-07-31; the merger documents and the third-quarter report would close it. - Low: carrying value by instrument is not disclosed, so principal is used and one aggregate issuance cost row reconciles to total debt; no source states the security or ranking of the finance leases of 0.8, which are left out of the debt stack; the lease agreements would close it. - Low: lines the statements print as a dash are treated as not supplied, not zero: impairment charge in FY2023, proceeds from sale of businesses in FY2025, share repurchases in FY2024, FY2025, Q1 2025 and H1 2025, proceeds from debt issuance, holdback payment, receivables change in Q1 2026, debt issuance costs in H1 2026, and the discontinued and held-for-sale balance sheet lines in 2026; the statements as filed carry no other source for these cells. - Low: lines that a period's statement does not print are not supplied for that period, for example the continuing and discontinued operations subtotals of the cash flow statement in the annual columns and the treasury stock line in the 2026-06-30 balance sheet; no action is needed. - Low: the 2025 balance sheet is kept as filed; the 2026 quarterly reports show it recast, with receivables of 412.6 against 417.7 and inventories of 335.9 against 424.2, while totals, cash and debt agree; a recast annual balance sheet would close it. - Low: income taxes paid and interest paid are stated only for the full years, so cash taxes are not shown for the interim periods; the third-quarter report would close it if it adds the disclosure. - Low: the maturity of the senior notes is stated by month only, April 2029 and August 2032, and no day is invented; the indentures would close it.

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Arcosa's credit risk now turns on a pending cash takeover by CRH: a change of control could cause a default or prepayment event under the credit agreement and both note indentures, and how the debt will be treated is not established. The operations are diversified and visible: utility structures backlog of USD 648.1 million supports 2026, wind tower backlog of USD 537.4 million fades as tax credits end after 2027, and one customer was 12.2% of 2025 revenue. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, and barge sale cash prepaid only USD 83.0 million of debt. Nothing dated after 5 August 2026 was supplied, so the shareholder vote scheduled for 4 September 2026 and the July amendment to the credit agreement are unresolved. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against treating the takeover as the dominant credit risk is that CRH is paying cash with no financing condition and has accepted a reverse termination fee of USD 372.0 million, larger than the USD 260.4 million Arcosa would owe, which points to completion by a strategic owner rather than a leveraged sponsor, and Arcosa holds USD 432.1 million of cash, enough for a 101% offer on the notes due 2029 of USD 404.0 million but not on both series, which would cost USD 1,010.0 million. The view would turn more negative if the debt documents show a Change of Control Triggering Event is likely or if the July 2026 amendment or the merger agreement added leverage or restricted creditors; it would turn positive if they show the notes and loans staying in place on unchanged terms or CRH repaying the credit agreement debt in full. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The change of control is the dominant credit question: the annual report warns that it could result in a default or prepayment event under each financing document, both note series carry a repurchase offer at 101% of principal on a Change of Control Triggering Event, and no source states what CRH intends for the debt. Repaying the term loan of USD 450.0 million and both note series at 101% would take USD 1,460.0 million, USD 327.9 million more than cash plus the whole USD 700.0 million revolver commitment, so the debt has to be refinanced, waived or left in place with CRH's support. The offer price implies an enterprise value of USD 8,370.6 million, so net debt is 12.00% of the value the buyer is paying, a wide equity cushion if the debt stays in place. facts.text: The strongest case against a cautious reading is that creditors sit under a wide cushion at the price the buyer pays: net debt is 12.00% of the USD 8,370.6 million enterprise value implied by the offer, the merger has no financing condition, and CRH has agreed to pay a termination fee of USD 372.0 million in specified circumstances, 5.05% of the equity value, against USD 260.4 million that Arcosa may owe. Cash of USD 432.1 million exceeds the notes due in 2029, nothing else falls due before then beyond USD 17.5 million of amortization, and the filings' own estimates put the notes due 2029 at 98.40% and the notes due 2032 at 104.45% of principal, from quoted prices in a thinly traded market. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Arcosa is a producer of infrastructure products whose continuing business has two segments after the barge sale: Construction Products at 51.47% of first-half revenue of USD 1,230.4 million, covering aggregates, specialty materials, asphalt and trench shoring, and Engineered Structures at 48.53%, covering utility, wind tower, traffic, lighting and telecom structures. facts.text: Overall, Arcosa presents an adequate business profile supported by a utility structures backlog of USD 648.1 million, local aggregates positions and net leverage of 1.97x, but credit quality is constrained by a change of control whose effect on the debt is not established, a wind tower revenue gap from 2028 and earnings growth that comes from gains. spans.text: # CP-0 Source readiness for Arcosa, Inc. (issuer-1739445), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Source readiness for Arcosa, Inc. (issuer-1739445), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The question is whether the four SEC filings supplied can support the financial foundation, the business and governance read and the fundamental credit view, and what is missing.
## Sources
No earlier module handoff was supplied; this module is the entry point. The run settings are not listed as a source.

| 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-27 (signature date) | 6fb40092bd7a9fb7c90415a6e54fcf75646d22f6e6c4284fff2b1126e5766878 | Latest audited statements and notes, the three-segment perimeter that still includes the barge business, the debt and covenant notes, and the exhibit index of the governing debt documents. |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_aca_aca-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-01 (signature date) | 6f3b02f51e836cdc7f032dfea160025a5c9a09b0b5df2bd8097f2bdc770050c6 | First quarterly statements recast for the discontinued barge business, the held-for-sale balances and the March 2026 revolver availability statement. |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-08-05 (signature date) | 1a77e9ef065b6dd943c2f4e6a5ef6e33bb8106ee089f7450954d028fe13735f0 | Latest period: statements, debt note, merger terms, barge sale completion, risk factors and exhibit list. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

The four filings support a dated credit read of Arcosa as of 30 June 2026 but not a current one, because nothing dated after 5 August 2026 was supplied and a cash takeover by CRH was then pending. For creditors that means leverage, liquidity and covenant headroom can only be stated as June positions: the shareholder vote scheduled for September, any third-quarter results, the July amendment to the credit agreement and the indentures behind the 101% change-of-control repurchase offer on the senior notes are all outside the evidence.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-02

The statements that were supplied are usable and tie to each other, but the 2025 annual figures still include the barge business that the 2026 quarterly reports treat as discontinued; it was 13.29% of 2025 revenue, so any trailing-twelve-month measure needs a rebuilt perimeter.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-03; calculation C-06; calculation C-09; calculation C-10

## Findings
### Bottom line

Arcosa's net leverage was 1.91x at 30 June 2026 on a continuing-operations basis, but that figure reflects barge sale cash held on the balance sheet, not earnings growth, so the creditor cushion is only as durable as that cash. Only USD 83.0 million of the USD 429.9 million net sale proceeds repaid debt, leaving USD 432.1 million of cash against USD 1,436.7 million of carrying debt, with a pro forma net leverage of 1.92x after the dividend paid on 31 July 2026. Continuing operations used USD 68.9 million of cash in the first half after capital expenditures, and cash interest cover for 2026 cannot be stated because the quarterly reports give no interest paid.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C-LB4; calculation C-N5; calculation C-B1; calculation C-X1; calculation C-F4; calculation C-X17
### Key findings

Net leverage peaked at 3.82x at the end of 2024 because the Stavola acquisition put its full financing on the year-end balance sheet while contributing only one quarter of earnings, then eased to 2.32x at the end of 2025 as earnings rose and USD 168.7 million of debt was repaid; the 2025 figure still includes a barge business that earned USD 53.6 million of EBITDA and has since been sold.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; calculation C-V2; calculation C-V3; calculation C-X6

Cash interest cover fell from 16.10x in 2023 to 7.81x in 2024 and 5.48x in 2025 as interest expense rose from USD 28.1 million to USD 108.8 million on the acquisition financing. The first half of 2026 carried USD 9.7 million less interest expense than the first half of 2025, which gives 5.30x of EBITDA over interest expense for the twelve months to June 2026; that is an accrual-based proxy, not cash cover.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C-I1; calculation C-I2; calculation C-I3; calculation C-P5; calculation C-X7

Earnings growth is modest: last-twelve-month EBITDA to June 2026 is USD 14.0 million, or 2.74%, above the 2025 figure rebuilt without the barge business, and 14.99% of first-half operating profit came from other operating income such as asset sale gains, so the debt reduction rests on disposal proceeds rather than on trading.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C-X17; calculation C-X14; calculation C-R4; calculation C-LB4

Cash flow quality is the weaker side: receivables rose USD 146.4 million in the first half of 2026, continuing operations used USD 68.9 million after capital expenditures against USD 43.1 million used a year earlier, and USD 84.7 million went on three acquisitions and USD 17.5 million on share repurchases, while investing cash flow was positive only because discontinued operations brought in USD 428.5 million. Over the full years operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 312.3 million in 2024 and USD 175.5 million in 2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation C-X13; calculation C-F2; calculation C-F3; calculation C-F4; calculation C-F5

Liquidity is ample on the balance sheet but incompletely evidenced: cash was USD 432.1 million at 30 June 2026 and the revolver commitment is USD 700.0 million with no loans outstanding, yet the June report states neither the undrawn amount nor letters of credit, so the facility figure for that date is left as not supplied. There is no debt maturity before the 2029 senior notes apart from the term loan amortization of USD 7.0 million a year.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-D1
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against the cautious reading is the size of the cash buffer: USD 432.1 million of cash and a USD 700.0 million revolver with no loans outstanding cover the 2029 notes of USD 400.0 million, and net debt fell by USD 303.6 million in six months. The view would improve if the third-quarter report shows operating cash flow covering capital expenditures and the proceeds still unspent; it would worsen if they were spent on acquisitions, buybacks or a merger-related payment, or if the amendment of July 2026 changed the covenants.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-X3; calculation C-N5

## Gaps
- High: no source is dated after 2026-08-05, so every ratio, balance and the merger outcome stop at 2026-06-30; the third-quarter report and the merger documents would close it.

- High: the 2025 annual report includes the barge business (revenue of 383.3, EBITDA of 53.6) while the 2026 quarterly reports and their 2025 comparatives exclude it; the last-twelve-months figures therefore use a 2025 year rebuilt from the segment note, which is a calculation, not a company figure; a recast annual statement would close it.

- High: the covenant leverage ratio, its EBITDA definition and the interest cover test level are not printed, so covenant headroom is not calculable; the credit agreement and Amendment No. 3 dated 2026-07-29 would close it.

- Medium: no cash interest paid is stated for the interim periods, so EBITDA over cash interest is not calculable for 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 and the proxy on interest expense is shown instead; the third-quarter cash flow statement or a supplemental disclosure would close it.

- Medium: the undrawn revolver amount and letters of credit are not stated at 2026-06-30, and the undrawn amount at 2023-12-31 is not stated, so those two liquidity cells are not supplied; the March 2026 statement of 700.0 is the latest.

- Medium: the issuer states no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or add-backs, so the EBITDA bridge is not stated and EBITDA is derived from operating profit and depreciation, depletion, and amortization; no source states a covenant EBITDA.

- Medium: the effect on net debt of the merger agreement, Amendment No. 3 and the proxy statement is not stated, so the post-balance-sheet table carries only the dividend of 2.5 paid on 2026-07-31; the merger documents and the third-quarter report would close it.

- Low: carrying value by instrument is not disclosed, so principal is used and one aggregate issuance cost row reconciles to total debt; no source states the security or ranking of the finance leases of 0.8, which are left out of the debt stack; the lease agreements would close it.

- Low: lines the statements print as a dash are treated as not supplied, not zero: impairment charge in FY2023, proceeds from sale of businesses in FY2025, share repurchases in FY2024, FY2025, Q1 2025 and H1 2025, proceeds from debt issuance, holdback payment, receivables change in Q1 2026, debt issuance costs in H1 2026, and the discontinued and held-for-sale balance sheet lines in 2026; the statements as filed carry no other source for these cells.

- Low: lines that a period's statement does not print are not supplied for that period, for example the continuing and discontinued operations subtotals of the cash flow statement in the annual columns and the treasury stock line in the 2026-06-30 balance sheet; no action is needed.

- Low: the 2025 balance sheet is kept as filed; the 2026 quarterly reports show it recast, with receivables of 412.6 against 417.7 and inventories of 335.9 against 424.2, while totals, cash and debt agree; a recast annual balance sheet would close it.
- Low: income taxes paid and interest paid are stated only for the full years, so cash taxes are not shown for the interim periods; the third-quarter report would close it if it adds the disclosure.
- Low: the maturity of the senior notes is stated by month only, April 2029 and August 2032, and no day is invented; the indentures would close it.

spans.text: # CP-1A Business & governance for Arcosa, Inc. (issuer-1739445), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Business, ownership, governance and transaction facts for Arcosa, Inc. (issuer-1739445), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is who owns and controls the issuer, what it does, how it behaves as a borrower and what transactions are pending, built from the four supplied filings.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_aca_aca-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-28 (signature date) | 009d98ca6402203c835c2f662f1f77d343ec31fe3235b25079eac2f28081685f | 2023 and 2024 history: acquisitions, divestitures, financing and the earlier covenant wording. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-27 (signature date) | 6fb40092bd7a9fb7c90415a6e54fcf75646d22f6e6c4284fff2b1126e5766878 | Business description, segments, customers, backlog, properties, executive officers, ownership and governance references, 2024 and 2025 transactions. |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_aca_aca-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-01 (signature date) | 6f3b02f51e836cdc7f032dfea160025a5c9a09b0b5df2bd8097f2bdc770050c6 | Barge sale held for sale, dividend declared February 2026, supplemental indentures and change-in-control plan exhibits. |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-08-05 (signature date) | 1a77e9ef065b6dd943c2f4e6a5ef6e33bb8106ee089f7450954d028fe13735f0 | CRH merger terms, barge sale completion, bolt-on acquisitions, revenue by business line, backlog, risk factors and the exhibit list. |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | Source readiness handoff for Arcosa, Inc. | 2026-11-18 (as-of date) | 863c814a2ac8eb6e03a56b5e8c78b6c23b3a2f0a2c0445b5518dc17df32d0ec7 | Source set, missing documents and the barge perimeter finding. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Arcosa's credit risk now turns on a pending cash takeover by CRH: a change of control could cause a default or prepayment event under the credit agreement and both note indentures, and how the debt will be treated is not established. The operations are diversified and visible: utility structures backlog of USD 648.1 million supports 2026, wind tower backlog of USD 537.4 million fades as tax credits end after 2027, and one customer was 12.2% of 2025 revenue. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, and barge sale cash prepaid only USD 83.0 million of debt. Nothing dated after 5 August 2026 was supplied, so the shareholder vote scheduled for 4 September 2026 and the July amendment to the credit agreement are unresolved.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-H1
### Key findings

The takeover terms favour completion: shareholders receive USD 150.00 in cash per share, about USD 7,366.0 million of equity value; the merger has no financing condition, although Arcosa lists CRH's ability to obtain financing among its risks; CRH would owe a termination fee of USD 372.0 million against USD 260.4 million payable by Arcosa; and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, but the vote result and the regulatory position after 5 August 2026 are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C-A1; calculation C-A2

The change of control is the open creditor question: the annual report warns that a change of control, as each financing document defines it, could result in a default or prepayment event under the credit agreement and under both note indentures, and both series of senior notes carry a repurchase offer at 101% of principal on a Change of Control Triggering Event; the indentures, the credit agreement terms and CRH's plans for the debt were not supplied. At 30 June 2026 the 2029 notes were valued at 98.40% of principal and the 2032 notes at 104.45%, so a 101% offer would sit above the market for the first and below it for the second if the trigger were met.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 133–137; calculation C-F1

There is no sponsor to underwrite and shareholder returns are small: the stock is publicly traded, no controlling holder is named in the annual report, dividends are USD 0.20 per share a year, and share repurchases were USD 17.5 million in the first half of 2026, small against net barge sale proceeds of USD 429.9 million, of which USD 83.0 million prepaid the term loan.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-H1; calculation C-H2; calculation C-H3; calculation C-H4

The business is diversified but not evenly resilient: without the barge business, aggregates-led Construction Products were 52.41% of 2025 revenue, concentrated in Texas and New Jersey at about 35% and 20% of segment revenue, and Engineered Structures 47.59%, of which utility structures 33.39% and wind towers 14.21%; the largest customer, in wind towers, was about 14.07% of that revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C-B2; calculation C-C1

Wind tower demand has a visible cliff while utility demand is rising: the tax credit for wind towers ends for sales after 2027, 66% of the wind backlog is due in 2027, and that backlog fell 14.40% in six months while the utility structures backlog rose 49.02%; the company is converting an idled wind tower plant to utility structures, expected to be operational in the second half of 2026.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C-E1; calculation C-H5

Capital allocation has been acquisitive and debt-funded, and disposals are now reversing it: Stavola cost USD 1.2 billion in cash in October 2024, Ameron USD 180.0 million in April 2024, three bolt-on aggregates acquisitions USD 84.9 million in the first half of 2026, while the 2024 steel components sale and the USD 450 million barge sale have narrowed the group to two segments.

Disclosure is adequate for a public issuer but will change on closing: the annual statements carry an unqualified audit opinion, yet completion of the merger would delist and deregister the stock, which ends the filings creditors now rely on unless the debt documents require reports, and board, ownership and pay disclosure sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against treating the takeover as the dominant credit risk is that CRH is paying cash with no financing condition and has accepted a reverse termination fee of USD 372.0 million, larger than the USD 260.4 million Arcosa would owe, which points to completion by a strategic owner rather than a leveraged sponsor, and Arcosa holds USD 432.1 million of cash, enough for a 101% offer on the notes due 2029 of USD 404.0 million but not on both series, which would cost USD 1,010.0 million. The view would turn more negative if the debt documents show a Change of Control Triggering Event is likely or if the July 2026 amendment or the merger agreement added leverage or restricted creditors; it would turn positive if they show the notes and loans staying in place on unchanged terms or CRH repaying the credit agreement debt in full.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation C-F2
### Limitations

- The proxy statement and the merger agreement were not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists rests on the annual report alone and would change if a beneficial owner holds a large block or if the board has special rights.

- Nothing dated after 5 August 2026 was supplied, so the conclusion that the takeover is still pending, and its expected closing in the first quarter of 2027, could be overtaken by the shareholder vote, regulatory decisions or a competing offer.

- The indentures and the credit agreement were not supplied, so the conclusions on the 101% repurchase offer and on what a change of control does to the term loan, revolver and notes are limited to what the filings summarise and would change once the defined terms are read.
- The governance reading covers structure, disclosure and documented behaviour only and does not assess individuals, so it changes no conclusion about management quality.

The pending merger would make Arcosa a wholly owned subsidiary of CRH Americas, Inc. for USD 150.00 in cash per share, about USD 7,366.0 million; the agreement is not conditional on financing and carries termination fees of USD 372.0 million payable by CRH and USD 260.4 million payable by Arcosa, with an outside date of 21 June 2027 that can extend by up to six months. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Arcosa's fundamental credit profile is adequate, with net leverage of 1.97x and USD 432.1 million of cash, but the outcome for creditors depends on the pending CRH cash takeover, whose effect on the debt is not established. A change of control could cause a default or prepayment event under the credit agreement and both note indentures, and repaying every instrument at closing would cost USD 1,460.0 million against at most USD 1,132.1 million of cash and revolver commitment. The 1.97x corrects the 1.91x in Financial foundation, whose EBITDA was USD 14.7 million too high; pro forma net debt after the dividend paid on 31 July 2026 is USD 1,007.1 million, also 1.97x.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-06; calculation C-08; calculation C-09; calculation C-21; calculation C-24
### Key findings

The change of control is the dominant credit question: the annual report warns that it could result in a default or prepayment event under each financing document, both note series carry a repurchase offer at 101% of principal on a Change of Control Triggering Event, and no source states what CRH intends for the debt. Repaying the term loan of USD 450.0 million and both note series at 101% would take USD 1,460.0 million, USD 327.9 million more than cash plus the whole USD 700.0 million revolver commitment, so the debt has to be refinanced, waived or left in place with CRH's support. The offer price implies an enterprise value of USD 8,370.6 million, so net debt is 12.00% of the value the buyer is paying, a wide equity cushion if the debt stays in place.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-21; calculation C-24; calculation C-26

Leverage is moderate at 2.81x total debt and 1.97x net debt on EBITDA of USD 510.6 million for the twelve months to June 2026, but the net figure rests on barge sale cash: only USD 83.0 million of the USD 429.9 million net proceeds, or 19.31%, repaid debt, and of the USD 303.6 million fall in net debt in six months USD 217.5 million is higher cash. This corrects Financial foundation, which subtracted the segment operating profit of USD 46.1 million for the barge business instead of the USD 60.8 million the annual report states and so overstated EBITDA by USD 14.7 million; before the sale proceeds the ratios at 31 March 2026 were 3.02x and 2.71x, not 2.93x and 2.63x. The same error put the barge business at 13.48% of 2025 operating profit in Source readiness, against 17.78%.

Segment operating profit rose 14.99%, led by Engineered Structures, but corporate costs rose 43.59% on acquisition and divestiture expenses, so first-half operating profit rose only 6.83%; this normalization is Analyst Judgement applied to this reading only and leaves the leverage figures unchanged.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a cautious reading is that creditors sit under a wide cushion at the price the buyer pays: net debt is 12.00% of the USD 8,370.6 million enterprise value implied by the offer, the merger has no financing condition, and CRH has agreed to pay a termination fee of USD 372.0 million in specified circumstances, 5.05% of the equity value, against USD 260.4 million that Arcosa may owe. Cash of USD 432.1 million exceeds the notes due in 2029, nothing else falls due before then beyond USD 17.5 million of amortization, and the filings' own estimates put the notes due 2029 at 98.40% and the notes due 2032 at 104.45% of principal, from quoted prices in a thinly traded market. The view would improve if the debt documents or CRH show the credit agreement debt repaid and the notes staying in place on unchanged terms, or if second-half cash flow after capital expenditures turns positive; it would worsen if a Change of Control Triggering Event is met while liquidity is below the call, if wind tower orders do not refill the 2028 backlog, or if first-half gains on asset sales prove to be the main source of earnings growth.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C-14; calculation C-22; calculation C-25; calculation C-26
### Limitations

- The credit agreement and the indentures were not supplied, so the conclusion that leverage is moderate is stated on reported EBITDA, not on the covenant measure that nets at most USD 150.0 million of cash against a 4.00x maximum, and headroom against that covenant would change the view of liquidity risk once it can be calculated.

- Continuing EBITDA is rebuilt from the annual segment note and the quarterly statements, not recast by the company, so the leverage of 1.97x would move one for one with any recast of the barge business figures or of the 2025 corporate costs.

- No profit is reported separately for wind towers and utility structures, so the conclusion that profit growth now depends on utility structures is a revenue-based reading and would change if wind tower margins differ materially from the Engineered Structures average.

- Only the first half of 2026 is supplied for cash flow, so the conclusion that cash generation is weak rests on the seasonally weakest period and would soften if the second half repeats the 2025 pattern.
- No peer set, market price or credit rating was supplied, so the adequate assessment of the profile is a judgement against the issuer's own history and the sources, not against comparable issuers.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The utility structures franchise is the clearest strength: a backlog of USD 648.1 million, up 49.02% since the year end and 71% due in 2026, comes from customers focused on grid reliability and sold partly through multi-year alliance contracts, so about USD 460.2 million of revenue is already ordered for the rest of 2026 against USD 456.0 million recognized in the first half; this supports revenue visibility and cash flow in 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-17

Balance sheet repair is a second strength: net debt of USD 1,004.6 million is 1.97x EBITDA, only USD 17.5 million falls due to 2028, and cash of USD 432.1 million exceeds the notes due 2029, which lowers refinancing pressure in the years before a possible change of control.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-07; calculation C-08; calculation C-22

Local aggregates positions are a third strength: Construction Products is 51.47% of first-half revenue, sold in markets where transport cost limits competing supply, with capacity utilization of 65% in both segments in 2025, which gives room for volume to lift profit without new plants; this supports margin stability.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C-29

The price and structure of the takeover are a fourth strength for creditors: net debt is 12.00% of the implied enterprise value and the buyer has accepted a larger termination fee, in specified circumstances, than the one Arcosa may owe, which supports completion and a wide equity cushion if the debt stays in place.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; calculation C-26

The change of control is the main weakness: each financing document may treat it as a default or prepayment event, the call on liquidity would be USD 1,460.0 million against at most USD 1,132.1 million, and the sources state neither the definitions nor CRH's intentions, so creditor outcomes are decided outside the evidence.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-21; calculation C-24

The wind tower cliff and customer concentration are the second weakness: backlog fell 14.40%, only USD 32.2 million is due in 2028, the tax credit ends after 2027 and one customer was 12.2% of 2025 revenue, which puts revenue and capacity absorption at risk from 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-17; calculation C-27

Weak cash generation and earnings quality are the third weakness: first-half free cash flow was a deficit of USD 68.9 million, capital expenditures rose 70.50%, and EBITDA before other operating income was flat, so deleveraging has depended on asset sales and the barge proceeds.

Opacity is the fourth weakness: ratings, covenant levels, guarantor lists and the July 2026 amendment are not in the sources, and a completed merger would delist the shares and end the filings creditors now use, so monitoring would depend on the debt documents.

### Company description

Arcosa is a producer of infrastructure products whose continuing business has two segments after the barge sale: Construction Products at 51.47% of first-half revenue of USD 1,230.4 million, covering aggregates, specialty materials, asphalt and trench shoring, and Engineered Structures at 48.53%, covering utility, wind tower, traffic, lighting and telecom structures. Aggregates and asphalt are sold locally, with Texas about 35% and New Jersey about 20% of 2025 segment revenue, to contractors and road agencies, while the structures businesses sell to utilities, turbine producers and state transport agencies, so cash flow follows public infrastructure budgets, housing and the wind tax credit rather than one commodity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-29

The portfolio has been reshaped twice in two years: the steel components sale in 2024, the debt-funded Stavola purchase for USD 1.2 billion that year, and the USD 450 million barge sale in April 2026. Business & governance describes the conversion of an idled wind tower plant to utility structures as expected in the second half of 2026; the June 2026 report says it has been converted and began delivering utility poles in the second quarter, and that a further wind tower plant will be converted in 2027, which supersedes the earlier wording.

### Ownership and group structure

Arcosa is a listed company with no controlling holder or sponsor named, so its financial policy is set by management and a board that a creditor cannot assess from the supplied filings; the proxy statement that would show board, holdings and pay was not supplied. The credit agreement and both note series are guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries that the filings do not name, the revolver and term loan are secured on substantially all personal property while the notes are unsecured, so the priority between them is by security, not by legal entity, as far as the sources state.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 113–115; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

If the merger closes, Arcosa becomes a wholly owned subsidiary of CRH and its shares are delisted and deregistered; creditors would then rely on the debt documents for information and on CRH's financial policy, which the sources do not describe. The offer of USD 150.00 per share implies equity of USD 7,366.0 million, and the fees of USD 372.0 million and USD 260.4 million show the buyer's commitment; neither establishes whether the debt is repaid, assumed or put back.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is partly visible and partly cyclical: first-half revenue rose 2.95% to USD 1,230.4 million, with utility structures up 13.72% and wind towers down 20.19%, and Construction Products up only 2.59%, where higher trench shoring revenue was the main driver and single-family housing weakness held back volumes. Utility revenue is supported by alliance contracts and a backlog of USD 648.1 million, wind tower revenue depends on a tax credit that ends after 2027 and on turbine producers, one of which was 12.2% of 2025 revenue, and construction materials depend on public funding, with a new surface transport authorization or an extension expected by the end of 2026, and on mortgage rates.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-16; calculation C-17

Pricing power is local for aggregates, because transport cost is high relative to product value, and contractual for structures, because price escalation clauses pass much of the steel cost to customers; competitive bids in utility structures cap price. For creditors that means margin is more resilient to input costs than to volume: a drop in orders or housing starts, not price, is the way revenue durability would fail.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11
### Cost structure and margin resilience

EBITDA margin was 20.14% for the twelve months and 19.74% in the first half against 19.15% a year earlier, but the improvement comes from gains on asset sales and Engineered Structures, whose operating margin rose to 18.72% from 14.05%, while Construction Products margin fell to 11.05% from 12.46%. Selling, general and administrative expense rose 16.95% and corporate costs 43.59% on acquisition and divestiture expenses, which hold reported EBITDA down and persist while the merger is pending, so the margin is held up by gains that may not repeat and held down by deal costs that may.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C-11; calculation C-14; calculation C-15

Margins can be defended against steel price moves through escalation clauses and flexing between steel types, and capacity utilization of 65% in Construction Products and Engineered Structures leaves room to add volume; they are less defensible against volume loss in wind towers, where fixed plant cost is spread over fewer units, which is the mechanism behind the sensitivity of USD 66.5 million of EBITDA in the downside scenario.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C-30
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital intensity has risen: capital expenditures were 8.31% of first-half revenue against 5.74% in 2025, and the plant conversions add growth capital, while receivables absorbed USD 140.1 million of cash in the first half and cash interest was USD 103.1 million in 2025. EBITDA converted to 31.07% free cash flow in 2025 including the barge business, and free cash flow of continuing operations was a deficit of USD 68.9 million in the first half; free cash flow available for debt service is therefore not yet established, and capital expenditure flexibility, with dividends of only USD 4.9 million in the half, is the main lever management has.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation C-18; calculation C-19
### Porter's Five Forces

Competitive rivalry is regional in aggregates and national in structures: the aggregates industry is highly fragmented and grows by acquisition, which supports local pricing but invites debt-funded roll-up, while structures producers compete on quality and delivery and, for utility work, in competitive bids; the risk to creditors is acquisition spending, not price war.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

The threat of new entrants is low in aggregates, where proximity to demand centres and permitted reserves act as barriers, and moderate in structures, where capacity can be converted, as Arcosa itself is converting wind tower plants; this protects aggregates margins and exposes structures margins to competitors that can also convert.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23

The threat of substitutes is limited for aggregates and asphalt, and recycled aggregates, of which Arcosa is the largest US producer, are a complement; for wind towers the substitute is a change in policy that removes the tax credit, which the 2025 law does for sales after 2027.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

Buyer power is concentrated in wind towers, where turbine producers are the main customers and one was 12.2% of 2025 revenue, and moderate in utility structures, where alliance contracts offset competitive bids; the effect is price and volume pressure on the wind tower line when orders slow.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-27

Supplier power is moderate: steel is the principal material for Engineered Structures, its price fell through 2025, and escalation clauses and flexing between steel types limit the effect on operating profit; supply was sufficient in 2025.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11
### PEST analysis

Policy and economic factors are material to credit quality; social and technological factors are not primary drivers on the provided materials. The 2025 law ends the manufacturing credit for wind towers sold after 2027, which sets the date of the wind tower revenue gap, and a new federal surface transport authorization is expected by the end of 2026 or an extension of the current one; interest rates and housing affordability held back residential volumes, with Texas housing permits down about 8% in 2025, which pressures Construction Products volumes. Demand for electricity, including from artificial intelligence projects, supports utility structure orders, which partly offsets the policy loss.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23
### SWOT analysis

Strengths in credit terms are the utility backlog of USD 648.1 million, net leverage of 1.97x with cash of USD 432.1 million, local aggregates positions with spare capacity, and fixed-rate notes that are 59.28% of interest expense. Weaknesses are the negative first-half free cash flow, earnings growth that comes from gains, concentration in one wind customer and an opaque debt structure.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C-08; calculation C-14; calculation C-18; calculation C-23

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the conversion of wind tower plants to utility structures, which redirects capacity to growing demand, and a buyer with a stronger balance sheet that leaves the debt in place. Threats are the wind tower credit expiry, the change of control provisions in the debt documents, housing weakness in Texas and the loss of public reporting after closing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months utility structures, with 71% of the backlog due in 2026 and 20% in 2027, and public infrastructure budgets in Texas and New Jersey are tailwinds, while the shift from wind towers, housing weakness and the merger's conduct restrictions are headwinds; net leverage is likely to stay near its current level unless the proceeds are spent or cash flow improves. Wind tower backlog would sustain 2027 revenue at about the 2025 level, USD 354.7 million against USD 355.2 million, then falls away, which is the first break in the medium-term outlook.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C-17

Over three to five years the credit depends on whether utility structures and aggregates volumes replace wind tower profit and whether the owner after the merger keeps the current financial policy; the sources support neither a positive nor a negative conclusion beyond 2027, and that is stated as not established rather than assumed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7
### Qualitative downside scenario

The issuer-specific downside begins with the end of the wind tower tax credit after 2027: with only USD 32.2 million of backlog due in 2028 and no replacement orders, wind tower revenue of USD 355.2 million in 2025 falls away, and one customer that was 12.2% of 2025 revenue stops being a source of volume. The first operational break is lost absorption at the wind tower plants, which cuts Engineered Structures margin; the financial transmission is lower EBITDA, and at the Engineered Structures margin of 18.72% the loss is about USD 66.5 million, 13.02% of EBITDA, taking net leverage to 2.26x, total leverage to 3.24x and interest cover to 4.48x with net debt held constant, an illustration that ignores utility growth and is Analyst Judgement.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-15; calculation C-17; calculation C-30

Liquidity would not be the first casualty: cash of USD 432.1 million exceeds debt falling due to 2029 of USD 424.5 million, and management can cut capital expenditures, reduce buybacks and dividends of USD 0.20 per share, and redirect plants to utility structures, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress from operations alone. The sharper path is combined: a change of control that triggers prepayment or the 101% offer when the revolver's availability is uncertain, because the call of USD 1,460.0 million would exceed liquidity of at most USD 1,132.1 million. The primary downside path is therefore a change of control that forces refinancing of the credit agreement debt before the wind tower gap shows in earnings, and the observable triggers are the vote and closing dates, any repurchase offer and the 2028 wind backlog.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C-21; calculation C-22; calculation C-24
### Overall credit view

Overall, Arcosa presents an adequate business profile supported by a utility structures backlog of USD 648.1 million, local aggregates positions and net leverage of 1.97x, but credit quality is constrained by a change of control whose effect on the debt is not established, a wind tower revenue gap from 2028 and earnings growth that comes from gains. Cash-flow durability appears adequate for debt service on the evidence of 2025, weak in the first half of 2026 and not established for the second half. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the debt documents' treatment of the merger, the revolver's availability and its August 2028 maturity, and CRH's financial policy. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indentures and Amendment No. 3, the vote and closing outcome, any report after June 2026, ratings, and profit by product line. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: a change of control that forces repayment or refinancing of the debt.
